'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Beirut clashes]]
**Six people are killed and 32 more are injured during a shooting at a protest in [[Beirut]], [[Lebanon]], against the judge investigating the [[2020 Beirut explosion|2020 port explosion]]. [[Hezbollah]] and [[Amal Movement|Amal]] accused the attackers of being members of the [[Lebanese Forces|Christian Lebanese Forces]]. Clashes occurred for hours afterwards between the [[militia]]s involving [[sniper]]s, pistols, [[Kalashnikov rifle|Kalashnikov rifles]] and [[Rocket-propelled grenade|rocket-propelled grenades]] even after the [[Lebanese Army|army]] was [[Military deployment|deployed]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-58901611 (BBC News)]
*[[Kongsberg attack]]
**The man accused of killing five people and injuring three more yesterday in the streets of [[Kongsberg]], [[Viken (county)|Viken]], [[Norway]], using a [[bow and arrow]], is identified as a 37-year-old Norwegian man and [[convert to Islam]] with [[Denmark|Danish]] citizenship, who police had been concerned about regarding radicalization. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/suspect-norway-bow-and-arrow-killings-is-danish-man-police-say-2021-10-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Four [[India]]n soldiers are killed during a gunfight with rebels in a forest in [[Mendhar Tehsil|Mendhar]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. [https://www.greaterkashmir.com/todays-paper/front-page/mendhar-encounter-2-missing-soldiers-found-dead-toll-4 (Greater Kashmir)]
*[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
**A [[Taliban]] police commander is killed and 11 more people are injured as a bomb targeting the commander's vehicle explode in [[Shaigal Aw Shiltan District|Shigal District]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.thedefensepost.com/2021/10/14/blast-kills-taliban-commander/ (The Defense Post)]
*The [[Nigerian Army]] confirms that [[Abu Musab al-Barnawi]], the leader of [[Islamic State – West Africa Province|ISWAP]], died two months ago. However, the circumstances of al-Barnawi's death are not clear. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58576635 (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Brazil]]'s [[Central Bank of Brazil|Central Bank]] sells [[US Dollar|US$]]1 billion to offset declines in the [[Brazilian real|real]], which has fallen ⅓ relative to the dollar in 2021 alone, with another US$1 billion in sales scheduled for later today. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/10/14/central-bank-of-brazil-takes-action-to-reverse-real-shrinking (Mercopress)]
*[[LinkedIn]] announces that it will shut down its social media services in [[China]] later this year, citing heavy-handed compliance requirements from the government, and will replace it with a traditional job-listing site. LinkedIn was the only major Western-based [[social media]] site to legally operate within the country prior to the announcement. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-58911297 (BBC News)] 

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Kaohsiung tower fire]]
**At least 46 people are killed and 79 others are injured in a fire at a 13-storey [[tower block]] in [[Kaohsiung]], [[Taiwan]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58887760 (BBC News)]
*Aftermath of [[Lion Air Flight 610]] and [[Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302]]
**A former [[Boeing]] chief [[test pilot]] is indicted by a [[Grand juries in the United States|United States grand jury]] for [[Tort of deceit|deceiving]] the [[Federal Aviation Administration]] during the [[Boeing 737 MAX certification|certification]] process for the [[Boeing 737 MAX]] aircraft, which resulted in two fatal crashes and a subsequent [[Boeing 737 MAX groundings|grounding of the aircraft]]. [https://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/latest-news/us-grand-jury-indicts-former-pilot-of-boeing-737-max/news-story/c696c4340797ca4c6582678e9574e453 (AFP via ''The Australian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Bali]] reopens its borders to fully vaccinated travellers from 19 countries that met [[WHO]]'s criteria as the number of COVID-19 cases declines in [[Indonesia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-business-lifestyle-java-indonesia-47a2c077023c5fa5fe0588847b8fcf1f (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports a record 15 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 207. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/23-year-old-and-34-year-old-with-multiple-underlying-medical-conditions-among-15 (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Vietnam]]
****The [[Vietnam]]ese [[Ministry of Health (Vietnam)|Ministry of Health]] approves [[vaccination]] against COVID-19 for children between the ages of 12 and 17 years old, with those aged 16 to 17 years old receiving priority before vaccination expands to other age groups. [https://en.vietnamplus.vn/covid19-vaccination-now-covers-children-aged-12-17-moh/209749.vnp (Vietnam Plus)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Latvia]]
****[[President of Latvia|President]] [[Egils Levits]] tests positive for COVID-19 after returning from a trip to [[Denmark]] and [[Sweden]] despite being fully vaccinated, prompting his [[President of Finland|Finnish counterpart]] [[Sauli Niinisto]] to self-isolate. [https://www.barrons.com/news/latvia-s-president-contracts-covid-despite-being-vaccinated-01634247307 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 986 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 220,315. The country also reports a record 31,299 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 7,892,980. [https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/72890/ (Interfax)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports a record 2,297 new cases and 11 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest daily total of any [[States and territories of Australia|state of Australia]] since the beginning of the pandemic. Victorian [[Premier of Victoria|Premier]] [[Daniel Andrews]] announces that the state will continue to reopen based on [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccination]] rates. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/oct/14/victoria-covid-update-state-on-track-to-reopen-despite-record-case-numbers-says-daniel-andrews (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
* [[China|Chinese]] Catholic Bishop [[Stephen Yang Xiangtai]], the retired leader of the [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Daming|Handan diocese]], died at the age of 99 after a long illness. Bishop Yang was arrested in 1954 and again in 1966, and served more than a decade in labor camps before being released in 1980. He became Bishop of Handan in 1999. [https://www.catholicculture.org/news/headlines/index.cfm?storyid=52565 (Catholic World News)] [http://www.asianews.it/news-en/Handan's-Bishop-Emeritus-Yang-Xiangtai-has-died-54278.html (Asia News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Armenia–Azerbaijan relations]]
**[[Armenia]] expands its case before the [[International Court of Justice]] against [[Azerbaijan]], accusing Azerbaijan of violating the [[International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination]], to which both states are signatories, for allegedly promoting [[ethnic hatred]] against [[Armenians]]. Azerbaijan denies the accusation and accuses Armenia of violating the [[treaty]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/armenia-tells-world-court-azerbaijan-promotes-ethnic-hatred-2021-10-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Murder of Giulio Regeni]], [[Egypt–Italy relations]]
**An [[Judiciary of Italy|Italian court]] in [[Rome]] drops [[criminal charge|charges]] against four [[Egyptian National Police|Egyptian police]] officers for the 2016 [[murder]] of Italian [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] student Giulio Regeni in [[Cairo]], citing its inability for the four officers to be [[Trial in absentia|tried in absentia]] since their prosecutors failed to inform them of their charges. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211014-italian-court-stops-trial-against-egyptians-over-student-s-murder (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Sri Lanka]] drops charges against Admiral [[Wasantha Karannagoda]], who was accused of being part of a group of 14 [[Sri Lankan Navy|navy]] personnel who [[kidnapping|kidnapped]] 11 children and murdered them after attempting to [[extort]] money from their families. The actual number of children murdered by the group is suspected to be at least three times higher. The crimes were carried out in 2008 and 2009, amid the chaos of the [[Sri Lankan Civil War]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/14/sri-lanka-charges-former-navy-chief-11-killings-civil-war-tamils (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Japanese general election]]
**[[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Fumio Kishida]] dissolves the [[House of Representatives (Japan)|lower house]] of the [[National Diet|Japanese Parliament]] ahead of the election on October 31. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2021/10/14/japan-fumio-kishida-dissolves-parliament-elections/6881634216659/ (UPI)]
*[[2021 Norwegian parliamentary election]]
**[[Jonas Gahr Støre]] takes office as [[Prime Minister of Norway]]. [https://apnews.com/article/business-denmark-europe-norway-9370dce582ddc667935c0c7208c5e31d (Associated Press)]
*[[Pakistan International Airlines]] suspends flights to the [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] capital [[Kabul]], citing "heavy-handed" interference from the [[Taliban]]. It was the only foreign carrier operating regular flights out of Kabul. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58913855 (BBC News)]
